item.title: 2027: We won’t endorse any candidate — Health workers
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — Ahead of the 2027 elections, the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN) on Wednesday declared that its members will not endorse or finance any candidate. The health workers also said they are rejecting a spectator role in the forthcoming elections and demanded binding commitments on CONHESS and outstanding arrears. Speaking in his welcome address at the 52nd session of the National Executive Council (NEC) meeting in Abuja, the President of the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria, Comrade Kabiru Ado Sani, said the union will enter the 2027 general election neither as party loyalists nor as passive observers, but as an organised constituency demanding enforceable commitments on welfare, CONHESS arrears, and outstanding collective agreements. In a strongly worded position ahead of the polls, the union said the question confronting health workers is no longer whether they will participate in the election, but on what terms. “The permutation is now upon us. The question is no longer whether health workers will be in it, but whether we shall be in it as spectators, as foot soldiers, or as a constituency with a strong position,” the MHWUN President said. He warned that health workers must not allow their numerical strength and professional importance to be reduced to election-season mobilisation for politicians who may abandon their concerns afterwards. MHWUN insisted that it remains a trade union, not a political party, and would not endorse any candidate or political platform. “MHWUN is a trade union, not a political party. We will not endorse any party or candidate, and the funds of this Union will not be used to finance any of them,” the union leader stated. He added that members remain free to vote according to their conscience, stressing that no individual has the authority to speak for the union while campaigning for a party. “Our members are free to vote their conscience, and no one speaks for this Union when speaking for a party,” he said. The union argued that its political influence should not depend on telling members whom to vote for, but on forcing every contender for power to confront the health sector’s unresolved demands. “Our influence does not lie in telling members how to vote. It lies in making the health worker’s agenda impossible to ignore, whoever wins,” the MHWUN political head declared. He explained that at the centre of that agenda are the CONHESS salary structure, unpaid arrears, and collective agreements reached with the Federal Government but yet to be fully implemented. The union framed its demands in legal as well as moral terms, insisting that agreements signed by the Federal Government cannot be treated as disposable political promises. “A collective agreement signed by the Federal Government is an obligation of the State,” Dr. Sani said. “It does not lapse when a tenure ends, and no incoming administration is entitled to treat it as the debt of its predecessor.” He wa

item.title: Nigeria can become Africa’s rice export hub — NGF
item.description: …Forum says 5.3m-tonne production deficit can be bridged, urges states to establish data banks By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) has expressed optimism that Nigeria can become a major rice exporter in Africa, insisting that the country’s agricultural potential and available human, financial and natural resources are sufficient to achieve the ambition. The forum said Nigeria could close its 5.3 million metric tonnes rice production deficit and become a net exporter if governments addressed policy inconsistencies, improved agricultural data and provided sustained support to farmers and other players across the value chain. The Director-General of the NGF, Dr. Abdulateef Shittu, stated this on Wednesday in Abuja during the launch of the Northwest Rice Diagnostic Report organised by the forum. Shittu said Nigeria currently consumed about 8.6 million metric tonnes of rice annually, a figure projected to rise to 9.1 million metric tonnes next year, while domestic production stood at only 3.3 million metric tonnes. He blamed the production shortfall on inconsistent government policies, poor coordination and other challenges affecting the agricultural sector. According to him, Nigeria has no justification for remaining dependent on imported rice, given its agricultural resources and capacity to supply regional African markets and parts of Europe. He cited China’s transition from food deficit to self-sufficiency through targeted investments, saying Nigeria needed similar political commitment to achieve food security. Shittu said: “You can see the huge gap. So, how do we address this? There are a lot of policy flip-flops, policy mismatch, and quite a number of other challenges that we will all have to address. But my motto simply is that there is no problem without a solution. “We have all the resources, both human and material. We have the land and everything that we need to support farmers and other actors across the value chain. Whatever they need can be guaranteed.” He described credible data as central to agricultural planning and disclosed that the NGF had established a dedicated data department to improve the collection and management of information across states. He urged all 36 states to establish functional Bureaus of Statistics, noting that Kaduna and some other states had already taken the initiative. According to him, national statistics, including Gross Domestic Product figures, should reflect aggregated data from the states and the Federal Capital Territory. The NGF boss said the forum was also challenging figures presented by development partners where it believed they were inaccurate. “If we are saying it is not correct, we have to show them which one is correct,” he said. He added that heads of State Bureaus of Statistics met quarterly under a committee of practice, while commissioners of agriculture also held periodic meetings to exchange ideas and experiences. item.title: Yusuf urges Nigerians to be patient with Tinubu’s policies
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf KANO — Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has urged Nigerians to be patient with President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, saying the difficult decisions taken by the administration are aimed at rescuing the economy and stabilising its macroeconomic environment. The governor said the policies had helped stabilise the economy, expressing optimism that the benefits would eventually translate into improved living conditions for Nigerians. Yusuf, who was represented by Muhammad Yusuf Jamu, spoke on Wednesday at the inauguration of campaign coordinators for the presidential, governorship, senatorial, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly elections in Tarauni Local Government Area of Kano State. He said the President had taken difficult decisions to address the country’s economic challenges, adding that economic stability would create a conducive environment for businesses to thrive. “The President’s economic policies have helped rescue the country’s economy and stabilise the macroeconomy. With a stable economy, businesses can go to the markets and carry out their transactions. “We are now at a stage where the economy is growing, and the microeconomy will soon begin to flourish, so that Nigerians can also feel the benefits. “We are in a period where tough decisions have been taken to rescue the country. We urge Nigerians to be patient with the President and his government’s policies. At the end of the day, we will all celebrate,” he said. The governor also urged members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kano to sustain efforts towards reconciliation and unity within the party ahead of the 2027 general elections. He called on party members to abide by established rules and work collectively towards the success of the APC. “I urge you to continue on this path of reconciliation and strictly adhere to the rules of the game. We have the best candidates to present to the people of Kano,” he said. He further urged party supporters to vote for the APC across all elective positions in the 2027 elections. “On election day, everyone should vote for the APC from top to bottom and from bottom to top,” he added. Also speaking, the APC candidate for Tarauni Federal Constituency, Hon. Nasir Bala Aminu Ja’oji, pledged to expand empowerment programmes and educational support for residents if elected in 2027. Ja’oji said education would remain his priority, alongside youth and women development, healthcare and economic empowerment. item.title: 5 facts to know about Keisha Lance Bottoms, America’s first black female governor
item.description: By Morenike Taire, Woman Editor Her historic victory in Georgia breaks a century-old political barrier for Black women in the United States. The United States has recorded another milestone in its political history following the election of Keisha Lance Bottoms as Georgia’s governor, making her the first Black woman elected governor of a US state. Bottoms, a former mayor of Atlanta, defeated Republican candidate Rick Jackson in the November 3, 2026 gubernatorial election. Her victory is particularly significant in a country where women and Black Americans have historically faced considerable barriers to political representation. Here are five things to know about the woman making history. She is the first Black woman elected governor of a US state Bottoms has broken a significant racial and gender barrier in American politics. Although several women have previously served as governors, no Black woman had ever been elected to lead a US state before her victory in Georgia. Her election represents a landmark moment for Black women in American public life and expands the history of women’s political representation in the country. She will assume office in January 2027. She is also Georgia’s first female governor Beyond making national history as the first Black woman elected governor, Bottoms will also become the first woman to occupy Georgia’s governorship. Her election marks a departure from the state’s political history, in which men have held the office since Georgia became a state. Interestingly, the United States elected its first female governor more than a century ago. Nellie Tayloe Ross of Wyoming became the first woman to take the oath of office as a state governor on January 5, 1925. Ross was elected in November 1924 following the death of her husband, Governor William B. Ross. She subsequently served until January 1927. The distinction is important: Ross made history as the first woman governor, while Bottoms has now made history as the first Black woman elected to the governorship of a US state. She was previously the Mayor of Atlanta Before her historic gubernatorial victory, Bottoms served as Mayor of Atlanta, Georgia’s capital and one of the most prominent cities in the United States. She held the position from 2018 to 2022, becoming a nationally recognised political figure during her tenure. Her mayoral administration coincided with major national developments, including the COVID-19 pandemic and the protests following the killing of George Floyd in 2020. Her experience in municipal leadership provided a platform for her subsequent return to national politics. She has experience in the White House Bottoms’ political experience extends beyond local government. item.title: 2027: Atiku Vows To Tackle Insecurity At Sokoto Campaign Flag-Off, Says Nothing Will Stop ADC
item.description: Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has reaffirmed his commitment to tackling insecurity, declaring that alleged attempts to frustrate his party’s campaign will not stop its activities ahead of the 2027 general election. Atiku spoke on Wednesday at the flag-off of his presidential campaign in Sokoto, where he urged Nigerians to support the ADC and vote for the party in the forthcoming election. His declaration came a day after he accused the Sokoto State Government and security operatives of plotting to disrupt the campaign rally, alleging that the Department of State Services (DSS) was recruiting protesters to cause disturbances and create a situation that could be used to impose a curfew. Crowd at the flag off of Atiku Abubakar campaign in Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. At a news conference in Abuja on Tuesday, the former Vice President also accused the state government of denying the ADC access to public facilities and logistical support for the rally. He described the alleged restrictions as deliberate attempts to deny the opposition party a level playing field. The DSS subsequently ordered an investigation into Atiku’s allegation, saying the directive was issued by its Director-General despite the Service describing the claim as inconsistent with its operations. In its response, the agency said its operatives had provided security protection to political actors across party lines. It cited an incident involving the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto, Mannir Daniya, whom its personnel reportedly evacuated to safety after he was attacked on October 31. Despite the controversy, Atiku proceeded with the campaign flag-off, saying no attempt to frustrate the party would deter it from addressing the people of Sokoto. Crowd at the flag off of Atiku Abubakar campaign in Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. He explained that the state was deliberately chosen for the campaign launch because of its historical significance and reputation for peace. The ADC candidate recalled the promises he made during his previous campaign, saying he had returned to reaffirm his commitment to those pledges, particularly his promise to tackle insecurity if elected president. He also called on Nigerians to turn out in large numbers on election day and vote for the ADC, expressing confidence in the party’s political mission. The rally marks the formal commencement of Atiku’s presidential campaign activities in Sokoto ahead of the 2027 general election. item.title: Oborevwori assures residents of peaceful elections
item.description: Gov. Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta has assured residents of the state of peaceful, free and fair elections. He also warned political parties against violence and urged all to respect the rule of law. Oborevwori gave the assurance at a stakeholders’ meeting on electoral security on Wednesday in Asaba. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the meeting is organised by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Represented by his Senior Political Adviser, Sen. Emmanuel Aguariavwodo, Oborevwori reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to providing a conducive political environment for all parties. According to him, all political parties are free to campaign and canvass for votes without intimidation or harassment. The governor also urged political parties to sell their programmes and ideas to the electorate through peaceful campaigns and other lawful engagements. He however, warned that anyone who violated the law would face the consequences, irrespective of political affiliation. Oborevwori while pledging the state government’s support for INEC and its Resident Electoral Commissioner in the state, noted that achieving credible elections required collective commitment from all. According to him, this include from the INEC, security agencies, political parties, civil society organisations and the electorate,” he said. He added that no single institution could deliver credible elections independently, urging all stakeholders to collaborate in preventing electoral violence. Also speaking, the state Commissioner of Police, Mr Samuel Erale, warned political parties and their supporters against violence, declaring that security agencies were fully prepared to enforce electoral laws. Erale said that the police would monitor political activities and maintain peace before, during and after the elections. “We want to be peaceful. We will be on ground. We will monitor all the activities of everyone,” he said. The CP said security agencies would provide a level playing field for all political parties to exercise their democratic rights within the provisions of the law. He warned that anyone who resorted to violence or breached electoral regulations would face the full weight of the law. “The moment violence is involved, you leave us with no choice than to come and do our duties,” he said. He stressed that maintaining peace, providing a level playing field and ensuring compliance with electoral laws were key priorities of security agencies. He added that no individual, political party or contestant would be exempted from enforcement of electoral laws. Erale also assured stakeholders that security agencies would not compromise their responsibilities, stressing their commitment to credible and transparent elections. He urged political stakeholders to cooperate with security agencies to ensure peaceful campaigns and a violence-free electoral process. item.title: Afenifere, Igbo forum seek stronger Yoruba-Igbo ties, back Tinubu, Hamzat
item.description: The Afenifere and Ndi Igbo Unity Forum have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening Yoruba-Igbo relations and promoting peaceful coexistence in Lagos State. Chief ​‌‍‍‍‍Deji Wellington, State Chairman of Afenifere, a Yoruba socio-cultural organisation, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, after a meeting with leaders of the Igbo community aimed at rebuilding cordial relationships between the two ethnic groups. Wellington said the initiative was designed to change the existing narrative and restore the cordial relationship that previously existed between the Yoruba and Igbo communities. He said it was important for Igbo residents to regard Lagos as their home and maintain peaceful relationships with their host community. “It is our desire that the Ndi Igbo (Igbo people) see Lagos as home, where they are expected to work peacefully with the host community. “They should establish good relationships with the Lagos State Government and subsequently protect their businesses, investments and properties,” he said. Wellington said stronger relationships between the Igbo community, the host community and the state government would promote mutual understanding, security and peaceful coexistence. He said the initiative was also aimed at creating an atmosphere where residents from both ethnic groups could pursue their economic interests without fear or hostility. Wellington said Igbo leaders had pledged their support for President Bola Tinubu’s second-term ambition and the 2027 governorship aspiration of Lagos State Deputy Governor and APC candidate Dr Obafemi Hamzat. He said the forum also promised to collaborate in mobilising support for Tinubu and Hamzat across the state. Wellington said the forum pledged to take the campaign to local government areas, wards and Igbo communities across the state. “The Igbo leaders have promised to join Afenifere in its determination to rally support for the President’s second term and Dr Hamzat as Lagos State Governor in the 2027 election,” Wellington said. He expressed optimism that the partnership would strengthen inter-ethnic relations, deepen political cooperation and promote a more peaceful and inclusive environment in the state. item.title: ₦70,000 Transport Allowance: Labour veterans wade into crisis between NLC, TUC
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — Labour veterans from the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) have intervened in the face-off between the President of the NLC, Comrade Joe Ajaero, and the TUC President, Comrade Festus Osifo. The two labour leaders have recently traded words over the recent approval of ₦70,000 by the Federal Government to cushion the effect of high transportation costs occasioned by the removal of fuel subsidy. The rift between the two leaders degenerated into personal attacks on national television, a situation that has affected unity within the labour sector. Worried by the development, labour veterans met to bring the situation under control. Speaking on Wednesday in Abuja at the 52nd session of the National Executive Council (NEC) of the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN), Comrade Wabba said the labour veterans had been able to arrest any form of hostility between the two leaders. The former NLC President told journalists that veterans from the two labour centres had met to resolve what he described as a family misunderstanding between the two centres. He said the veterans emphasised that workers’ organisations must remain united because they share a single objective and aim. The former President of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC) said all hostilities had been ordered to stop, explaining that the goal is to prevent future occurrences through formal dialogue. He said: “It’s a family misunderstanding between the two centres, and we have made it clear that workers’ organisations are supposed to be one because the objective is one and the aim is one. “So, that seeming misunderstanding has escalated, and we have said all hostilities should stop. We will actually try to meet with them to see what happened and how future occurrences can also be prevented. “So, basically, I can tell you for sure that veterans from both sides—TUC and NLC—namely Peter Esele, Bobboi Kaigama, Hassan Sunmonu, Abdulwaheed Omar, and my humble self, actually met and tried to look at the issue. We said we would meet formally when all of them are available because we just communicated among ourselves, the veterans, and we communicated with them, and they mutually accepted. “The TUC General Secretary was here; I was here; the NLC President was here. All of us embraced ourselves and said, ‘Well, it’s a family issue.’ Therefore, we have also said members of the press should not actually try to advance issues that are not there because, even in your immediate family, you can have some internal issues. “But that internal issue is certainly meant to be resolved, and we are working towards that very effectively because that is the hallmark of trade unionism: to resolve issues, even with our employers, through dialogue and social dialogue. item.title: NNPC posts N3.49trn profit in nine months
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja ABUJA — The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) recorded a cumulative Profit After Tax (PAT) of N3.494 trillion between January and September 2026, following an 18.1 per cent increase in its September profit to N509 billion. The September profit rose from N431 billion recorded in August, according to the company’s September 2026 Monthly Operations and Financial Report. The latest figures bring NNPC’s cumulative profit for the first nine months of 2026 to N3.494 trillion. A breakdown of the performance showed that the company recorded profits of N385 billion in January, N136 billion in February, N276 billion in March, N481 billion in April, N462 billion in May, N535 billion in June, N279 billion in July, N431 billion in August and N509 billion in September. The report also showed that NNPC generated N33.152 trillion in revenue during the nine-month period. Its September revenue stood at N4.608 trillion, representing a 23.3 per cent increase from the N3.737 trillion recorded in August. Monthly revenue figures showed that the company generated N2.571 trillion in January, N2.680 trillion in February, N2.774 trillion in March, N4.971 trillion in April, N4.335 trillion in May, N4.389 trillion in June and N3.087 trillion in July. On its statutory obligations, NNPC disclosed that payments to the Federation Account and other statutory remittances rose to N11.14 trillion between January and September. The amount represents an increase of 17.4 per cent, or N1.65 trillion, over the N9.49 trillion recorded between January and August. On the operational front, average crude oil and condensate production stood at 1.70 million barrels per day in September. Natural gas production also increased to 7,789 million standard cubic feet per day, compared with 7,680 million standard cubic feet per day recorded in August. Total hydrocarbon production, comprising crude oil, condensate and natural gas equivalent, averaged 3.04 million barrels of oil equivalent per day during the period. The company further reported 100 per cent availability of its upstream pipeline infrastructure in September. On gas infrastructure projects, NNPC said the Obiafu-Obrikom-Oben (OB3) Gas Pipeline had achieved 100 per cent completion, while the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) Gas Pipeline was 95 per cent complete. It added that the OB3 River Niger Crossing pipeline had been commissioned and operationalised. According to the company, collaboration with relevant stakeholders was ongoing to accelerate construction and pre-commissioning activities on the AKK project, with a target of delivering early gas supply to Abuja before the end of 2026. item.title: Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State Police Command on Wednesday arrested a 27-year-old man, Victor Edet Yellow Duke, in connection with an attack on the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, in Calabar, the state capital. The attack left the windshields of some vehicles smashed. The incident occurred at about 2:20 p.m. at the Watt Market Roundabout as the convoy was returning from the palace of the Obong of Calabar to Metropolitan Hotel, the venue of the party’s presidential town hall meeting. According to the police, a group of suspected hoodlums, reportedly armed with machetes and sticks, emerged from the Calabar Road and Clerks Alley axis and attacked vehicles in the convoy. The number of vehicles affected had not been ascertained. Police personnel deployed in the area moved in swiftly to contain the situation. Their intervention, which included the use of tear gas, led to the arrest of the suspect, while the other attackers fled. The suspect was later taken to the State Police Headquarters by operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit, VCRU, for what the command described as a discreet investigation, to prevent reprisals or a further breakdown of law and order. Normalcy has since returned to the area. In a statement by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, the command said the Commissioner of Police, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, had ordered a thorough investigation to identify and arrest other participants and establish the full circumstances of the incident. Cautioning against presuming the suspect’s guilt, the police said: “The arrest of a suspect does not amount to a determination of guilt, as the suspect remains entitled to the presumption of innocence pending the conclusion of investigation and any subsequent judicial proceedings.” The command assured residents, political stakeholders and visitors that adequate security measures remained in place across the state. It reiterated its commitment to “providing equal security protection to all political parties, candidates and their supporters, irrespective of political affiliation.” It also urged the public to stay calm, avoid spreading unverified information and report suspicious activities through established police channels. Eitokpah added: “The Cross River State Police Command remains committed to maintaining public safety, protecting democratic participation and ensuring that all lawful political activities are conducted in a peaceful and secure environment.” The post Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Atiku vows to restore fuel subsidy, reopen borders, reduce pilgrimage costs
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to restore petroleum subsidy, tackle insecurity, reopen Nigeria’s land borders with neighbouring countries and reduce pilgrimage fares for Muslim and Christian faithful if elected president in 2027. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), made the pledges on Wednesday during the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto, where he outlined his proposed measures to address the country’s economic challenges, insecurity and declining standard of living. He said his administration would prioritise the welfare of Nigerians, adding that restoring petroleum subsidy would be among the measures considered to ease the burden of rising fuel prices and reduce transportation costs and the prices of essential commodities. The former vice-president also promised to take decisive steps to address insecurity across the country, protect lives and property and restore confidence in the nation’s security architecture. He said Nigerians deserved to live and conduct their businesses without fear of attacks, kidnapping and other criminal activities. On the economy, Atiku pledged to reopen Nigeria’s land borders with neighbouring countries to revive economic activities, strengthen regional trade and improve the livelihoods of communities dependent on cross-border commerce. He said the move would create opportunities for traders, farmers and other economic operators while strengthening Nigeria’s commercial relations with neighbouring countries. The ADC candidate also promised to reduce pilgrimage fares for Muslim and Christian faithful, arguing that the cost of religious journeys should not constitute an overwhelming burden for ordinary Nigerians. He said his proposed administration would introduce policies to improve citizens’ welfare, expand economic opportunities and address the hardship confronting households. Atiku urged Nigerians to support the ADC in the 2027 presidential election, saying the party would provide an alternative direction for the country. item.title: Peter Obi storms Calabar for NDC town hall as supporters throng airport, streets
item.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, on Wednesday arrived in Calabar, the Cross River State capital, ahead of the party’s presidential town hall meeting with stakeholders and supporters, to a rousing reception by party leaders and loyalists. The former Anambra State governor landed at the Margaret Ekpo International Airport, Calabar, in the afternoon, where party faithful had converged to receive him. He was welcomed by top NDC leaders in the state, party stakeholders and a large crowd of supporters who chanted solidarity songs and displayed party flags and banners. From the airport, Obi’s convoy moved through major streets of the Calabar metropolis amid cheers from supporters and residents, a development that caused a brief traffic gridlock along the route. Obi is expected to attend the presidential town hall meeting organised by the NDC at Metropolitan Hotel, Calabar, where he will interact with party members, stakeholders and residents on his plans for the country ahead of the 2027 general election. Security has been beefed up around the venue and other strategic locations in the metropolis. item.title: Oyebanji warns commissioners against arrogance, corruption
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, has warned newly inaugurated commissioners and special advisers against arrogance, indiscipline, corruption and abuse of office, declaring that his administration would not tolerate unethical conduct or inefficiency. He charged the appointees to remain humble, accountable and committed to delivering quality service to the people, warning that bureaucratic delays and careless mistakes capable of undermining the state’s development agenda would not be condoned. Oyebanji gave the warning on Wednesday in Ado-Ekiti during the inauguration of three commissioners and 10 special advisers into the State Executive Council. The new commissioners are Dayo Apata, SAN, Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice; Akintunde Oyebode, Commissioner for Finance; and Dr Oyebanji Filani, Commissioner for Health and Human Services. The 10 special advisers are Prof. James Olaleye, e-GIS, Lands and Survey; James Folorunso, Bureau of Public Procurement; Dr John Moyo Ekundayo, Office of Transformation, Strategy and Delivery; Bunmi Talabi, Bureau of Special Projects; and Olayinka Oyebode, Chief Press Secretary and Special Adviser on Media. Others are Princess Adetoun Agboola, Special Education and Social Inclusion; Dr Gbenga Oyewole, Development Planning and Budget; Kayode Adaramodu, Economic Affairs and Private Sector Development; Ebenezer Boluwade, Agriculture and Food Security; and Prof. Akeem Azeez, Special Duties. The governor said the inauguration, coming barely two weeks after the swearing-in of the Secretary to the State Government and other key officials, was aimed at ensuring that his second-term administration commenced without delay. He said the second term was not an opportunity for complacency or self-indulgence but a period to consolidate the achievements of the first term and accelerate the state’s development. Oyebanji particularly cautioned returning commissioners against allowing their experience and length of service to create a false sense of indispensability. “I would also like to counsel you to resist the temptation of the illusion of invincibility and indispensability, which could ultimately breed arrogance. At the end of the day, only God is truly indispensable. “We must all therefore remain gracious and wholeheartedly dedicated to our unwavering service to the good people of Ekiti State,” he said. He declared that he would be impatient and intolerant of indiscipline, unethical behaviour and corruption, insisting that all government activities must reflect professionalism, transparency, technical competence and efficiency. item.title: Senate advances Agricultural Revolution Bill
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — A bill seeking to establish a comprehensive legal framework for the transformation and modernisation of Nigeria’s agricultural sector has scaled second reading in the Senate. The bill, sponsored by the Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Jibrin Barau (APC, Kano North), seeks to promote food security, agricultural productivity, mechanisation, irrigation, agricultural financing, agro-industrialisation, rural development and climate-resilient farming. Following its passage at second reading, the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, referred the proposed legislation to the Senate Committees on Agricultural Production, Services and Rural Development, and Agricultural Colleges and Institutions for further legislative consideration. Akpabio directed the committees to report back to the Senate within four weeks. The bill, titled, A Bill for an Act to Provide a Comprehensive Legal Framework for the Transformation and Modernisation of Agriculture in Nigeria, is also designed to promote sustainable agricultural development and address longstanding challenges in the sector. Leading the debate on its general principles, Barau lamented that agriculture, which was once the mainstay of Nigeria’s economy, was no longer performing optimally. He recalled that between the 1950s and early 1980s, agricultural production supported numerous industries, including textile and processing companies in Lagos, Kano and Port Harcourt. He regretted that several industries, particularly those in Kano’s Sharada and Bompai industrial areas, which once supported vibrant economic activities, had become largely dormant. Barau also recalled that the Second Republic government introduced the Green Revolution Programme but noted that its implementation lacked an enabling legal framework. According to him, the absence of legislation made it difficult to sustain the programme beyond the administration that introduced it. He said Nigeria had the human and natural resources required to transform agriculture but lacked effective mechanisms to harness the sector’s enormous potential. “The bill is to provoke conversation, bring in our expertise to look at the entire scenario and see how we can change the trajectory,” he said. Barau urged senators to consider the proposed legislation from the perspective of patriotism rather than partisan politics, stressing the need for collective action to reposition the agricultural sector. Contributing, the Senate Whip, Senator Mohammed Monguno (APC, Borno North), said the bill would translate Nigeria’s economic diversification policy from oil dependence to agriculture into practical reality. He said agriculture contributed about 40 per cent of Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product and provided approximately 70 per cent of employment. item.title: 2027: Otti wave enough to secure re-election — Abia LP
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The Labour Party (LP) in Abia State has dismissed suggestions that the growing political influence of former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, could threaten Governor Alex Otti’s re-election chances in 2027, insisting that the governor enjoys sufficient grassroots support to secure another term. The party said the political momentum behind Otti, which it described as the “Otti wave”, was strong enough to withstand opposition and guarantee victory for the Labour Party in the state. There have been suggestions that Obi’s popularity and influence played a significant role in Otti’s victory in the 2023 governorship election and could again determine the outcome of the 2027 poll. However, the Publicity Secretary of the Labour Party in Abia, Chief Emenike Iroegbu, said the party had established a strong grassroots presence across markets, motor parks, local government areas and wards, making it confident of winning all elective positions in the state. Speaking in Umuahia, Iroegbu acknowledged Obi’s political stature but maintained that his influence would not undermine the Labour Party’s position in Abia. He noted that Otti had remained in the Labour Party while the party continued to strengthen its political structures across the state’s 184 wards and 17 local government areas. “What is currently driving political support for the Labour Party in Abia is the ‘Otti wave’. The ‘Otti wave’ is strong enough to withstand any opposition ahead of the 2027 polls. This is the ‘Otti wave’ that has been spreading like wildfire in the 17 LGAs of Abia State,” he said. Iroegbu claimed that candidates of other political parties, including the National Democratic Congress (NDC), All Progressives Congress (APC) and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), had been associating themselves with Otti’s popularity through campaign posters and social media posts. He added that the influence of the former Anambra governor was not strong enough to weaken the Labour Party’s political base in Abia. The party spokesman also expressed confidence that its grassroots structures would translate into electoral victories across the state in 2027. On the inclusion of politicians who served in previous administrations in the party’s campaign structures, Iroegbu defended the move, saying political parties should remain open to individuals willing to join and contribute to governance. He argued that admitting such politicians into the Labour Party did not represent a departure from the principles and policies of the Otti administration, insisting that the governor remained firmly in control of his government. item.title: NMDPRA warns of risks from Ogun illegal refinery
item.description: …EFCC traces discovery to whistleblower’s tip, surveillance By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) has warned that products from an illegal refinery uncovered in Ogere-Remo, Ikenne Local Government Area of Ogun State, could pose serious risks to vehicles, automobile engines and public safety. The authority gave the warning on Wednesday during an inspection of the facility jointly conducted with operatives of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). The Ogun State Coordinator of NMDPRA, Dr Atilola Akinyemi, said the facility, which occupies more than three hectares of land, had no operating licence or permit from any regulatory agency and was operating outside the supervision of relevant authorities. He disclosed that the facility had an underground storage tank with an estimated capacity of more than 90,000 litres. Akinyemi described the installation as a crude and illegal operation, saying its structures and equipment appeared designed to replicate the processes of a conventional refinery without complying with the required regulatory, technical and safety standards. “The facility you see here is very crude and completely illegal. This is not a refinery by any standard. This facility does not have a permit from any regulatory authority, and its operations are unknown to the relevant authorities,” he said. He explained that intelligence gathering by the EFCC was instrumental to the discovery, noting that routine regulatory monitoring alone might not have exposed an operation of such magnitude. “This kind of discovery cannot be made through ordinary monitoring alone; it requires intelligence gathering. As the Zonal Director of the EFCC has explained, intelligence was instrumental in uncovering this operation. We need more of such efforts,” he said. According to him, preliminary investigations showed that the facility had designated sections for receiving feedstock, storage, heating, processing and cooling. Other installations discovered during the inspection included underground heating systems, water hydrants for cooling, locally fabricated storage tanks, separation silos and other equipment used in petroleum processing. Akinyemi likened the operation to illegal refining activities that characterised parts of the Niger Delta in the 1990s and early 2000s, questioning the source of the crude materials allegedly being processed at the facility. “One question that comes to mind is: where do they source their feedstock?” he queried. He said the equipment and general layout suggested that the operators had some technical knowledge but had established the facility outside the country’s petroleum regulatory framework. item.title: UNICEF raises polio alert in Niger, detects five cases
item.description: ….Three human infections, two environmental samples identified in Bida, Chanchaga By Clare Nnabuike, Minna The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has raised the alarm over the detection of five polio cases in Niger State, urging residents to intensify surveillance and ensure that children receive routine immunisation against the disease. The five detections comprised three cases identified through human samples and two through environmental surveillance in Bida and Chanchaga Local Government Areas of the state. UNICEF called on residents, parents and community leaders to support vaccination campaigns and sensitisation efforts to prevent further spread of the virus and achieve a polio-free environment. The agency raised the alarm on Wednesday during a mass mobilisation dialogue organised in collaboration with the Niger State Primary Health Care Development Agency. Speaking at the event in Minna, UNICEF’s representative in Niger State, Mrs Grace Odeyemi, urged residents to strengthen disease surveillance and community engagement, particularly in the affected local government areas. She stressed the need for parents to ensure that their children received polio vaccines, describing immunisation as essential to preventing the disease. Odeyemi explained that health officials routinely monitored children with paralysis or symptoms resembling those of polio victims, collecting samples for laboratory testing to establish the actual cause. She said surveillance also involved environmental sampling to detect the virus even when no infected individual had been identified. “We still carry out routine immunisation of the population. We are vaccinating the children to ensure that we eradicate the disease from the state. “We sample humans, that is, any child that we find in the community with paralysis, having a similar feature of polio-affected victims. “We quickly notify our local surveillance officers to collect samples for tests to see if it is polio or something else that is actually causing the paralysis because it’s not only polio virus that causes paralysis,” she said. She disclosed that the virus had been detected through both human and environmental surveillance in Chanchaga and Bida, bringing the total detections in the state to five. The Niger State Immunisation Officer, Abubakar Usman, said routine and emergency vaccination exercises had been intensified to protect children in the affected communities. He disclosed that reactive vaccination had been conducted in areas where the virus was detected to prevent further transmission. Usman said the agency had also embarked on community engagement involving traditional leaders and other intervention groups to educate residents on the dangers of rejecting immunisation. He attributed the detections largely to poor routine immunisation coverage and non-compliance by some parents and caregivers. “The virus was detected in the state. item.title: Soludo has awarded 908km of roads since 2022 — Commissioner
item.description: …Ezeobi says 442km asphalted, less than 5km affected by failures By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Government has awarded contracts for the construction of 908.44 kilometres of roads across the state since Governor Chukwuma Soludo assumed office in 2022, the Commissioner for Works, Architect Okey Ezeobi, has said. Ezeobi, who disclosed this while addressing journalists in Awka, said 442 kilometres of the roads had been fully asphalted, describing the administration’s road construction programme as unprecedented in the state’s history. He claimed that the combined road construction achievements of the three previous governors fell short of the number of kilometres asphalted by the Soludo administration. According to him, the government has awarded 143 road contracts since taking office. Addressing complaints on social media about the condition of some roads constructed by the administration, the commissioner said the affected portions amounted to less than five kilometres out of the 442 kilometres asphalted. “Of all the 442 kilometres of road we have asphalted, if you cut the portions that failed as a result of the effects of underground water, they are not up to five kilometres. That means that we have over 95 per cent of all the roads constructed by this administration in perfect condition,” he said. Ezeobi attributed some of the reported road failures to underground water, unusually heavy rainfall and blocked drainage channels, insisting that the government was addressing the affected sections. He alleged that some residents deliberately blocked drainage channels to allow sand to accumulate for harvesting and commercial sale, thereby worsening flooding and damaging public infrastructure. The commissioner explained that some roads remained in good condition until the recent heavy rainy season, which he said exposed the effects of underground water that had not been adequately captured in the initial construction data. “Many of the roads were designed and built and they never became bad until this year’s heavy rainy season. It’s the underground water that is the cause of the road damage, as the data we used did not capture the volume of the underground water,” he said. He added that the effects of underground water were also visible in residential buildings, where ground-floor surfaces were reportedly peeling. On allegations of poor construction standards and the engagement of unqualified contractors, Ezeobi maintained that the government had carefully selected reputable construction firms to handle its projects. He described the contractors as A-rated companies, saying they had the capacity to return to sites and carry out reconstruction whenever defects occurred. According to him, the affected contractors were undertaking the repairs at no additional cost to the state government. item.title: Tambuwal accuses APC of failing Nigerians
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto Former Sokoto State Governor, Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of failing Nigerians, citing worsening poverty, hunger and insecurity across the country. Tambuwal made the allegations at the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto, where he urged Nigerians to support the opposition party as an alternative to the ruling APC. Addressing party supporters at the rally, the former governor said the APC had failed to provide the leadership needed to address the country’s economic and security challenges. He argued that millions of Nigerians were grappling with worsening economic difficulties, widespread hunger and persistent insecurity, which he said had exposed the ruling party’s inability to govern effectively. Tambuwal maintained that Nigerians deserved a government capable of guaranteeing security, economic stability and better living conditions. He urged citizens to embrace the ADC, describing the party as an alternative capable of addressing the country’s pressing challenges. The former governor’s remarks came amid intensifying political exchanges ahead of the 2027 general elections. He called on Nigerians to rally behind the ADC and its presidential candidate, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, to change the country’s political direction. item.title: Tinubu Departs Saudi Arabia For Nigeria After Umrah
item.description: President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday departed King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, for Abuja after completing his Umrah (Lesser Hajj) in the holy city of Makkah. According to a statement by the presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, the President’s aircraft took off from the Royal Terminal of the airport at exactly 5:13 p.m. Saudi time. Onanuga said the Deputy Governor of the Makkah Region, Prince Saud bin Mishal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Nigeria’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and the Consul-General, Muazam Ibrahim Nayaya, accompanied the President to the airport. Before his departure, Tinubu held a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah at the Royal Guest Palace within the airport. ﻿ The President had earlier led members of the Nigerian delegation in performing the Umrah rites, including the circumambulation of the Holy Ka’abah. Last Sunday, Tinubu was granted the rare privilege of entering the sacred structure, where he and members of his delegation performed the two raka’at prayers. Inside the Holy Ka’abah, the President offered special supplications to Almighty Allah for lasting peace, security, unity and prosperity in Nigeria, while seeking divine guidance, wisdom and strength to continue serving the Nigerian people. He also prayed for Allah’s continued blessings upon Nigeria, its leaders and citizens, expressing hope that the country’s diversity would become a source of strength, national cohesion and shared prosperity. Tinubu held a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah at the Royal Guest Palace within the airport before departing Saudi Arabia. Onanuga said the President’s visit to Saudi Arabia provided an opportunity for spiritual reflection, thanksgiving and prayers for Nigeria, as well as a renewed commitment to building a peaceful, united and prosperous nation. The statement added that Tinubu expressed profound appreciation to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for the special courtesies and hospitality extended to him and the Nigerian delegation, particularly the privilege of accessing the Holy Ka’abah to offer prayers. “President Tinubu left the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia with renewed faith, gratitude to Almighty Allah and an unwavering commitment to the Renewed Hope Agenda and the aspiration of building a better Nigeria for all,” the statement said. Those in the President’s entourage included the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, and the governors of Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Borno and Yobe States, among others. item.title: Lagos Opens Legal Research Centre, Targets Stronger Justice Delivery
item.description: The Lagos State Government has opened a Centre for Legal Study, Research and Training, describing it as a strategic investment to strengthen the justice system, develop legal expertise and prepare the state’s justice institutions for emerging challenges. Established by the Lagos State Ministry of Justice, the Centre is expected to serve as a hub for legal research, professional training, policy development and capacity building for practitioners and public officials in the justice sector. Speaking at the official opening ceremony in Alausa, Ikeja, on Wednesday, the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Lawal Pedro, SAN, described the facility as more than another government building, saying it represents a deliberate investment in knowledge, institutional excellence and the future of justice administration in Lagos State. “There are occasions when we open a building or office. There are other occasions when we open a door to the future. Today, in Lagos, we are doing the latter — opening a door to the future,” Pedro said. He described the Centre as the first of its kind within a Ministry of Justice in Nigeria, arguing that a justice system that intends to remain relevant and effective must continually educate, examine and reform itself. Dignitaries at the opening of the Centre for Legal Study, Research and Training in Lagos. Pedro said the initiative aligns with the broader development agenda of the Sanwo-Olu administration, noting that the development of Lagos cannot be separated from strong institutions and an efficient administration of justice. He identified the rule of law, access to justice and capable institutions as essential foundations for economic development, good governance and social inclusion. The Attorney-General also linked the Centre to the administration’s THEMES Plus Agenda, stressing that building a secure, economically vibrant and inclusive society requires sustained investment in the people and institutions responsible for interpreting, administering and developing the state’s laws. He said the Centre would help address the growing demands of a modern justice system, including the need for continuous professional development, evidence-based policy and institutional reform. Outlining its proposed operational framework, Pedro disclosed that the Ministry intends to incorporate the Centre as a not-for-profit entity under a public-private partnership arrangement. Under the proposed structure, the Ministry of Justice and its private-sector partners will jointly manage the Centre’s day-to-day operations. While the government will provide policy direction, legitimacy and strategic oversight, the private sector is expected to contribute funding, technical expertise, innovation and operational efficiency. Pedro said the arrangement was designed to ensure the Centre’s sustainability and effectiveness. The Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Lawal Pedro, SAN. item.title: US Midterm Voters Deliver Brutal Verdict On Trump
item.description: Donald Trump faced a radically transformed and hostile political landscape on Wednesday after US voters handed control of Congress to the Democrats in a stunning rebuke to his presidency. The result was a personal humiliation for the 80-year-old Trump as a Democratic wave swept into his Republican heartland, boosted by anger at soaring energy costs and his costly, dragging war with Iran. The Democratic capture of both the Senate and the House of Representatives signals an end to Trump’s stranglehold on US politics and gives Democrats the power to block legislation, launch investigations into Trump’s administration and thwart his appointments. The results reflected deep frustration over the cost of living, tariffs and Trump’s war with Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. “This is so incredibly exciting. We can get our country back,” Kathy Jackoway said in Texas, celebrating a win by Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico. Trump struck a conciliatory tone despite his history of rejecting election defeats, telling The New York Times he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results. “I think the Democrats did a good job,” the 80-year-old told Fox News, in rare praise for his political opponents. “They fought hard.” Combo image of Democratic US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (r) and President of the U.S Donald Trump (l) But he sought to distance himself from his party’s poor showing, adding: “I don’t view it as a hit on me.” He acknowledged that the Iran conflict had contributed to the result but defended the military campaign, and he suggested the rival parties could find common ground on immigration. Republican Heartland Democrats flipped seats that had long been held by Republicans, scoring breakthroughs in South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Texas and Maine. In Maine, former logger Troy Jackson defeated longtime Republican Senator Susan Collins. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton became the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008. In Texas, Democrats won not only a Senate seat but also the governor’s race, ending decades of Republican rule. Democrats protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire. In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers, making him the first Muslim elected to the upper chamber of Congress. El-Sayed won despite a last-minute curveball when congresswoman Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to El-Sayed, came out in support of Rogers. In the House, Democrats made gains in Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Arizona, North Carolina, Wisconsin and New Jersey, including districts Trump had carried comfortably in 2024. item.title: How military reduced nationwide attacks by 73 per cent in October as 217 terrorists neutralised
item.description: Troops of the Nigerian military have drastically reduced attacks across various theatres of operations in October 2026, Daily Trust reports. Checks showed that only 98 attacks were recorded during the month under review, representing a 73.3 per cent decline from the 367 attacks recorded in September. A breakdown of the October figures showed that Operation Enduring Peace recorded the highest number of attacks with 29 incidents, followed by Operation Hadin Kai with 27 and Operation Fansan Yamma with 24. Operation Whirl Stroke recorded 12 attacks, while Operation Udo Ka recorded four. Operations Delta Safe and Savannah Shield recorded one attack each. Specifically, the October figure represents a decline of 269 attacks compared with the previous month’s total of 367. This is just as the Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, assured Nigerians that the military would intensify efforts to apprehend those responsible for the attacks and bring them to justice. Oluyede also urged troops to remain disciplined, uphold the rules of engagement and respect human rights, while warning against complacency, particularly as the festive season approaches. He called on security agencies to strengthen intelligence sharing and joint planning, while urging community leaders and residents to report suspicious activities to security formations or through the military’s toll-free line, 193. Providing updates for Nigerians on military operations across the country, the Director, Defence Media Operations, Major-General Michael Onoja, revealed that many kidnapped victims would continue to be freed from captivity. “During the period under review, the AFN recorded a total of 98 attacks across various theatres of operation. Operation HADIN KAI recorded 27 attacks, Operation FANSAN YAMMA recorded 24, Operation ENDURING PEACE recorded 29, Operation WHIRL STROKE recorded 12, Operation UDO KA (OPUK) recorded 4, while Operation DELTA SAFE and Operation SAVANNAH SHIELD recorded 1 attack each,” the breakdown was contained in a document released on Friday. Earlier in September, Operation Enduring Peace recorded 147 attacks, Operation Fansan Yamma 115, Operation Whirl Stroke 55, Operation Hadin Kai 33, Operation Savannah Shield 13 and Operation Udo Ka four, while Operation Delta Safe recorded none. The senior military officer explained that troops neutralised more than 217 terrorists and criminals, arrested 333 suspects and rescued 349 kidnap victims during the month. He added that 70 insurgents surrendered to troops, while 105 arms and 3,174 rounds of ammunition were recovered.
